questions.question: What combines multiple propositions into one?
What is a proposition that is true in some rows and false in others of its truth table called?
questions.explanation: A contingency is true under some assignments and false under others.

questions.question: What represents a single statement with no operators?
What evaluates truth values of propositions?
questions.explanation: Truth tables show all possible outcomes.

questions.question: What is the hypothesis in an implication?
What is the conclusion in an implication?
What operator means if and only if?
What term describes a conditional that is true because its antecedent is false?
questions.explanation: When the antecedent is false, the implication holds vacuously.

questions.question: What is the converse of the implication p→q?
questions.explanation: The converse swaps the hypothesis and conclusion.

questions.question: What do you call the operands p and q of a disjunction p∨q?
questions.explanation: Each operand of a disjunction is a disjunct.

questions.question: In the statement 'p is sufficient for q', which variable is the antecedent?
questions.explanation: Sufficient conditions occupy the antecedent position: p→q.

questions.question: What is the classification of the proposition (p→q)∨(q→p)?
questions.explanation: If one implication is false, the other is true, so the disjunction is always true.
